messages:
maria: Heads up — Kepler (dedicated pool kepler-prod) started getting sustained 429s around 2026-03-17T09:12Z during a marketing send. Customers reporting timeouts and increased latency.

jon: I see it in the dashboards too. burst_credits dropped to 0, admission controller began rejecting at ~09:13 UTC. Spikes look like a ~10k request burst over ~30s. :grimacing: 

maria: Sample logs (sensitive fields redacted):
```
[09:12:07] req_id=abcd-1234 status=429 reason=admission_throttled model=redwood-v2 tokens=120 tenant=8572
[09:12:07] admission=headroom=0.0 burst_credits=0.0 window_tps=450 allowed_tps=300
[09:12:08] req_id=abcd-1235 status=429 reason=admission_throttled
```

rachel: Customer says they fired a campaign that sent ~10k quick requests. They used the hosted client with their dedicated key. Can we repro and confirm whether auth/billing played a role or if this is purely admission headroom?

nate: Quick triage notes: autoscaler observed pressure and started adding nodes at 09:16, but node warmup + model load added ~20s. Admission is token/burst-based so burst credits were exhausted before new capacity came online. Autoscaler cooldown is currently 120s.

li: Repro steps I used locally (safe env):
1) Run loadgen: `k6 run --vus 200 --duration 60s` against kepler-staging with tenant headers.
2) Watch metric `redwood_admission_headroom` and `redwood_burst_credits`.
3) Observe `admission_throttled` spikes when credits hit 0.

(Logs attached to thread)

sam: I checked billing: burst credit refill job for tenant 8572 failed at 09:10 with upstream error (503 from credit-service). ops-bot posted ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-9241 (billing pipeline lag).

ops-bot: billing refill job failed for tenant 8572 at 2026-03-17T09:10:12 UTC — upstream-credit-service 503 — retry scheduled.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Manual top-up of burst credits for kepler to stop immediate 429s.
- Switch tenant to soft-fallback policy (allow smaller, cheaper model) while capacity scales.
- Consider a temporary increase in admission window for this pool.

jon: Doing manual top-up now. Command I ran: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://internal-api/tenants/8572/topup -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"credits":50000}'
```
jon: response: `{ "status": "ok", "new_balance": 50123 }`

ops-bot: Manual top-up succeeded for tenant 8572 at 2026-03-17T09:20:03 UTC.

rachel: Kepler confirms 429s dropped after the top-up and they see latency back to baseline by 09:22. They still want a postmortem and a prevention plan.

nate: Engineering action items I propose:
- Short-term: add a reactive prewarm hook when admission_pressure > 0.7 to reduce warmup lag.
- Mid-term: decrease autoscaler cooldown from 120s -> 30s for dedicated pools flagged for campaigns.
- Add an admission controller metric alert (headroom <= 0.1 for >10s) to create an automated ops runbook.

li: Also recommend: campaign guardrail doc for customers (recommended tps burst limits, pre-notify for scheduled blasts), and a safe default soft-fallback model to preserve availability.

maria: I'll open a support postmortem and tag eng-runtime + billing. Planning to include reproduction steps and the load test script for the e2e suite.

support-bot: Action items recorded: SUP-3721 (manual top-up), ENG-8192 (autoscale cooldown), DOCS-224 (campaign guardrail).

rachel: Customer happy for now, will schedule a follow-up meeting tomorrow. Closing this Slack thread but keeping tasks open. :white_check_mark:
